description:
We are Space Dragons, and we noticed that Earth and deep space are full of massive problems waiting to be solved. So we decided to swoop in and create solutions with our sharpest weapons: creativity, design, and code!

We are an interdisciplinary squad of AS/A-Level students from Heuser College, combining science, business, humanities, and tech to turn NASA’s open data into solutions that could actually make a difference.
summary:
My Little Moonbase is developed by SpaceDragons to complete the Build a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer challenge. This interactive survival game lets children play as an astronaut. Players begin by designing their astronaut, choosing an age and role (Explorer, Engineer, Scientist and Medic). Then they head off on with their dragon adventure buddy! The journey launches across the stars, where kids dodge asteroids and budget oxygen levels.

Once established on their lunar and Martian outposts, they have to complete 20 different missions to earn rewards and keep their ship safe. Using real NASA DONKI data to model planetary weather and temperature conditions, tasks simulate authentic deep-space survival trade-offs, including mapping lost spaceships on Mars, testing planetary atmospheres, matching star coordinates, tuning communications with Mission Control, repairing electrical systems, recycling water, analyzing lab samples, and managing crew health at the med bay and eatery stations.

This project addresses the challenge by turning competing survival demands into engaging gameplay. My Little Moonbase is important because young learners often struggle to picture how complex space systems work together. By blending real aerospace engineering and NASA space weather data into an enjoyable learning experience, the game builds early STEM problem-solving and critical thinking, inspiring young explorers to understand how astronauts survive beyond Earth.
details: Developed by SpaceDragons, My Little Moonbase is a browser-based space survival game built with HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and a secure Supabase backend (with development assistance from Claude). Designed for kids aged 7 to 12, the game lets players customize an astronaut, choosing their age and role (Explorer, Engineer, Scientist, or Medic), along with an adventure buddy, before piloting a spacecraft past asteroids and budgeting oxygen to land on the Moon. Before entering any planet, players view an information chart displaying real NASA DONKI space weather and temperature conditions so kids understand the environment ahead of time. Once on their lunar and Martian outposts, players complete 20 hands on missions for cash rewards, tackling tasks like mapping lost Mars spaceships, testing atmospheres, matching star coordinates, tuning Mission Control, fixing wires, recycling water, analyzing lab samples and running the med bay and eatery. Inspired by the playful, task-based style of Among Us, our team designed the game to feel fun, creative, and approachable without overstimulating graphics, keeping all options close and easily accessible so kids get to know life beyond Earth while building early STEM confidence.
